prose: Simon Willison asked Claude Opus 5.5 in the phone app to build a three.js game called Tree Appreciator, in which you compare two procedurally generated trees. After about three hours of work it returned a cozy spot-the-difference game with music, animation and achievements.
His takeaway is a little embarrassing to him: telling the model to make sure it is fun works better than it should.
highlights: Claude built a tree-comparison browser game in about three hours.
